transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. I guess… I’ve just been feeling really wound up most of the time. Like my body is bracing for the next bad thing, even when nothing is actually happening. It can be when I’m just sitting at my desk at work, or even trying to enjoy dance night, which is supposed to be fun. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been hard to just feel settled.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Yeah… I think there was something that kind of set it off. It’s been about nine months now, around when the condo loan started moving toward foreclosure. I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but that’s when I noticed I wasn’t really settling back down the way I used to. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or physical panic that peak within minutes?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like a sudden “attack” that peaks really fast, at least. I do get anxious, but it feels more like it builds or just kind of stays there, if that makes sense. I’m not sure if I’m answering that the right way.
Do you mainly feel this anxiety when you might be watched, judged, or evaluated by other people?

I don’t think it’s mainly that, no. I mean, I don’t love being judged—who does—but the anxious feeling doesn’t seem limited to situations with other people watching me. It can happen even when I’m just by myself. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, not just the condo foreclosure?

Yeah… I guess it has kind of spread out beyond the condo. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m worrying about everything all the time, but it jumps around a lot—like whether my cousin is upset with me, or if I’m going to mess up on a support call at work, or how I’m ever going to save money and move forward. So… yes, it’s not just the foreclosure, I think.
Have you been feeling down or depressed a lot lately?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I’ve felt kind of worn down and discouraged at times, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being “down a lot.” I’m trying to keep functioning, so… maybe a little, but I don’t want to overstate it.
If the foreclosure situation were fully resolved, do you think this anxiety would mostly go away?

I’d like to think it would, honestly. It would definitely help. But… I don’t think it would mostly go away completely, because my worry doesn’t really stay on the condo anymore. It kind of jumps around—to whether my cousin is upset with me, or if I’ll make a mistake on a support call, or how I’m ever going to save money or move forward. So I guess… no, not entirely. Is that what you mean?
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worry?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try to be reasonable with myself, like, “You already checked the spreadsheet,” or “You already sent the email, it’s fine.” But the thought doesn’t really stop there. It kind of keeps looping, and then one “what if” turns into five more before I can pull myself back.

I don’t know if that counts as hard to control, but… it feels like I can’t always shut it off when I want to.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge a lot lately?

Yeah… I think that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I feel wound up a lot of the time, like my body is sort of bracing for the next bad thing.

Even if I’m just sitting at my desk, or I’m supposed to be relaxing—like at dance night—I can still feel kind of on edge. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most days?

Um… I wouldn’t say depressed most days, no. I mean, I get discouraged and kind of worn down sometimes, but I don’t know that I’d call it sad or depressed in that way.

I don’t want to understate it, but… it feels more like stress than sadness, if that makes sense.
Have you been getting much less interest or enjoyment from things you usually like to do?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I still like the things I usually like… maybe I’m not always as relaxed during them as I want to be, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest or enjoyment.

Like, if I make myself go do something, I can usually still enjoy it. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling this anxious more days than not for at least six months?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not every single day all day, but more days than not, yes.

It’s been about nine months, I guess—since the condo loan started moving toward foreclosure. I kept thinking it would calm down once I got a handle on things, but it hasn’t really. Does that count as long enough?
Have you been feeling easily fatigued lately?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do get tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than what anyone would feel with everything going on. I can still get through my day, mostly. So… maybe a little, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
Do you feel your anxiety is much stronger than would be expected for the foreclosure situation?

I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, because the foreclosure is a real thing to worry about… but, yeah, maybe it’s gotten bigger than that.

It doesn’t really stay on the condo anymore. It jumps around—like I’ll start worrying whether my cousin is upset with me, or whether I’m going to mess up on a support call, or how I’m ever going to save money and move forward. So… I guess it does feel stronger than just the foreclosure, if that makes sense.
Is this anxiety making it hard for you to function at work, socially, or in other parts of daily life?

Um… yeah, a bit. I mean, I’m still going to work and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart. But I have started falling behind on support tickets, and I catch myself double-checking really simple things over and over. Sometimes coworkers have had to help pick up the slack, which I feel bad about.

And socially… I’ve skipped a few dance nights and mentoring sessions because I just felt too overwhelmed to show up. I know that probably isn’t ideal. So, yes, I guess it is getting in the way more than I’d like to admit.
Do you still get this anxious even at times when there isn’t anything specific going wrong or any immediate problem to think about?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to say it’s for no reason, because I can usually find something to attach it to if I think hard enough. But even when nothing is actually happening, I still feel kind of wound up, like my body is bracing for the next bad thing.

Even just sitting at my desk, or when I’m supposed to be enjoying dance night, there’s this tension there. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, I think it happens even without an immediate problem.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things that are unrelated to the foreclosure?

Yeah… I think I do. I mean, the foreclosure is still the big thing, obviously, so I don’t want to act like I’m just worrying out of nowhere.

But it doesn’t really stay on the condo anymore. It’ll jump to whether my cousin is upset with me, or whether I’m going to make some mistake on a support call, or how I’m ever supposed to save money and move forward. It’s like my brain just keeps finding another thing to latch onto. Is that what you mean?
Has the anxiety stayed closely connected to the foreclosure situation, or does it now feel more separate from that stress?

I guess it started with the foreclosure, but… no, it doesn’t feel like it stays neatly connected to that anymore.

It kind of jumps around now. Like I’ll be worrying whether my cousin is upset with me, then whether I’m going to mess up on a support call, then how I’m ever supposed to save money or move forward. I know some of that is probably normal to think about, but it feels like my brain keeps looking for the next thing. Does that make sense?
Do you feel your anxiety is mostly tied to the foreclosure stress, or does it feel like a general pattern of worry now?

I think… it’s more of a general pattern now, if I’m being honest. The condo is still part of it, but my worry doesn’t really stay there anymore.

It’ll jump around — like, whether my cousin is upset with me, or whether I’m going to make a mistake on a support call, or how I’m ever supposed to save money and move forward with my life. I know those are real things to think about, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it feels like my mind keeps finding something new to worry about.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control anxiety and worry occurring more days than not for about 9 months, spreading across multiple life domains beyond the initial foreclosure stressor. Associated symptoms clearly include restlessness/on-edge feeling, and there is functional impairment at work and socially. Panic attacks, social-evaluative restriction, and a primary depressive syndrome were not supported. Although symptoms began after a stressor, the anxiety has generalized beyond that event, favoring generalized anxiety disorder over an adjustment disorder.
